name: White House AI Policy Releases: Executive Orders, OMB Guidance and Federal AI Use
title: White House AI Policy Releases: Executive Orders, OMB Guidance and Federal AI Use
answer: The White House publishes executive orders, fact sheets and remarks setting federal AI policy. The most useful item for government readers is the April 2025 fact sheet on two revised Office of Management and Budget policies, M-25-21 and M-25-22, which reshape how agencies adopt and buy AI: Chief AI Officers become innovation advocates, agencies produce AI adoption maturity assessments, and a single high-impact AI category triggers heightened due diligence.

sections.body: This is the official White House website, whitehouse.gov, read across 60 pages on 3 October 2026. The pages reviewed are presidential actions, fact sheets and news releases issued between April 2025 and February 2026. They cover executive orders on AI education and on state AI law, a fact sheet on federal AI use and procurement, and remarks by Director Michael Kratsios at the APEC and India AI summits. The material is primary source policy text from the executive branch, not analysis or commentary.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The April 2025 fact sheet announces two revised Office of Management and Budget policies, M-25-21 and M-25-22, issued with the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology. M-25-21 gives agencies tools to adopt AI while protecting privacy, civil rights and civil liberties. Chief AI Officer roles are redefined as change agents and AI advocates rather than overseers of bureaucracy, tasked with promoting lower risk AI adoption, mitigating higher-impact risks and advising on AI spending. Agencies must produce an AI adoption maturity assessment. A single high-impact AI category tracks use cases needing heightened due diligence over rights or safety. Accountability mirrors existing government IT processes rather than new approval layers. M-25-22 guides agencies to acquire best-in-class AI quickly, competitively and responsibly. Separately, a December 2025 order directs the Attorney General to establish an AI Litigation Task Force within 30 days to challenge state AI laws inconsistent with national AI dominance, and the Commerce Secretary to publish an evaluation of state AI laws within 90 days, citing a Colorado algorithmic discrimination law. An April 2025 order creates a White House Task Force on AI Education and a Presidential Artificial Intelligence Challenge.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the AI Litigation Task Force must be established within 30 days and the state law evaluation published within 90 days. The education order requires a Challenge plan within 90 days and the event no later than 12 months after that plan. It defines AI by reference to 15 U.S.C. 9401(3). Kratsios said America's four largest AI companies plan to spend nearly $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year, and that more than three quarters of the billion users of leading American AI platforms log on from outside the U.S. Google committed $1 billion to U.S. education and job training, $150 million in grants over three years, and free Gemini for Education access for every American high school. IBM will skill 2 million learners by 2028, and Pearson offers up to 250,000 free certification vouchers.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For anyone following AI in government, this is the primary record of the rules federal agencies now work under. The OMB policies define how agencies govern, assess and procure AI, including the high-impact category and the recast Chief AI Officer role. The litigation task force and state law evaluation signal federal pressure on state AI regulation, which matters to vendors and agencies operating across jurisdictions. The education order and challenge create programmes agencies and contractors may deliver against. The summit remarks state the administration's positions on adoption, trust and sector-specific regulation.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Government

sections.body: This is executive branch communication, so it presents policy intent and supportive statements rather than independent evaluation. The releases quote industry leaders and organisations endorsing the administration's plans, and the remarks by Director Kratsios are advocacy for the American approach. The pages do not report implementation results, spending outcomes or measured effects of the OMB policies. Coverage is partial: the reviewed pages address education, procurement, state law and diplomacy, not operational deployments. Dates run from April 2025 to February 2026, so later changes are not reflected.
